- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 periods to account for volatility decay.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 3+ periods, apply upward bias of 1–3% per period to reflect mean reversion toward higher levels.  
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (±0.2) and forecast deviates >3% from true, apply smoothing: reduce forecast by 1–2% per period to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 2+ consecutive periods, assume upward bias and adjust next forecast by +1–2% to reflect trend continuation.
